preferential amplification can be significantly reduced by using a low annealing temperatures, but that the choice of the primers is also of great importance.
primer mismatch and annealing temperature are the major causes of preferential amplification in bacterial community analysis by 16S rDNA-targetting PCR.

the use of a lower annealing temperature (e.g. 50-55 degrees C) in combination with a primer that is perfectly matched to the target sequence is recommended to significantly reduce preferentially amplification of 16S ribosomal DNA in multitemplate PCRs, and thus to improve the reliability of 16S-based microbial community analysis.
